Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-10
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Leon Park (Redwood SE), Amira Khan (Celestia - Head of Partnerships), Diego Alvarez (Celestia - Cloud Architect), Priya Nair (Celestia - VP Strategic Alliances)

Auto-generated summary (auto):
- Intro + partner fit discussion between Redwood and Celestia Infra.
- Celestia is exploring reseller/partner integration for managed GPU capacity focused on enterprise customers in EMEA/APAC.
- Key concerns: data residency, dedicated capacity, integration model (resale vs reference arch), SLAs, and performance baseline for 8k+ token workloads.
- Next steps: share partner one-pager, security docs, run a technical deep dive and initial benchmarking plan.

Topics: partner model, reseller vs marketplace, dedicated pools, VPC peering, KMS/HSM, SOC2, benchmarks (latency/cost), sales motion.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Thompson: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood. Um, quick intro from us and then we'd love to hear about Celestia's GTM and what you're after.
[00:12] Amira Khan: Hi, thanks, Maya. I'm Amira, I run partnerships at Celestia. We provide managed GPU infrastructure across EMEA with a focus on enterprise compliance and localized data centers. We've been talking internally about expanding our partner catalog for inference platforms.
[00:25] Leon Park: Hi Amira, Leon here, I'm a solutions engineer — I focus on performance and deployment topologies. Quick question up front: are you thinking reseller (you operate and bill) or more of a reference/integration where we list you as an option?
[00:40] Priya Nair: Good question. We're open to both. For some regulated customers they want Celestia-managed instances (we'd resell), for others a marketplace listing is fine. The main ask is predictable SLOs and enterprise security.
[00:55] Diego Alvarez: Also, we need clarity on private deployment options. We get requests for VPC-hosted control plane or fully air-gapped on-prem racks. How flexible is Redwood's private offering?
[01:10] Maya Thompson: Great — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem. There's a private control plane option where customers keep networking and keys, and we can ship an on-prem package. For partners, we have a dedicated partner integration flow — we can support reseller contracts and marketplace listings.
[01:30] Amira Khan: Nice. Can you outline the typical integration work? Is it mostly API wiring, or do you need deeper infra access for things like KV cache and kernel optimization?
[01:44] Leon Park: Usually it starts with API integration and auth (SSO/service accounts), then we collaborate on private deployment config. For performance-sensitive workloads we do a kernel and quantization pass — but partners don't need to own that, we can do it jointly or provide tuned images for your fleet.
[02:05] Priya Nair: What about SLAs? Our sales org asks for 99.9 availability for dedicated customers. Can Redwood guarantee that for Dedicated / Reserved pools?
[02:18] Maya Thompson: Our Dedicated product comes with SLA-backed targets. We commit to uptime and latency bands on reserved capacity contracts; specifics depend on the contract tier and region. We can include this in partner playbooks.
[02:33] Diego Alvarez: Security checklist — customers ask about SOC 2, ISO, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations, and data locality. Can you share compliance artifacts?
[02:47] Maya Thompson: Absolutely. We'll send SOC 2 and our security overview. For KMS, we support external KMS integrations and can operate with customer-managed keys. Audit logs and request-level traces are available via the console.
[03:05] Amira Khan: Good. For the reseller model, we need to know margins, e.g., partner-discount tiers and lead routing. Is pricing negotiable per region?
[03:17] Maya Thompson: We have partner pricing tiers and volume-based discounts. We'll share the partner pricing sheet after this call. Typically discounts are tied to committed monthly reserved capacity.
[03:28] Leon Park: On the technical side — Diego, can you share a bit about typical workloads? Sequence lengths, tokens per call, and concurrency? That determines batching and kernel selection.
[03:40] Diego Alvarez: For a couple anchor customers, they run 8k token chat contexts with ~20 RPS at peak per tenant — but we see burst patterns, and some inference is real-time low-latency. They're sensitive to both tail latency and per-token cost.
[03:58] Leon Park: That's helpful. For 8k contexts we suggest using model variants with KV cache optimizations and continuous batching with short timeouts for low-latency paths. We'll prepare an initial cost/latency estimate based on that profile.
[04:15] Priya Nair: Does Redwood support multi-tenant isolation — e.g., per-customer dedicated pods?
[04:22] Leon Park: Yes, Dedicated pools can be carved per customer and isolated at network and storage levels. We also provide per-route quotas and tracing.
[04:30] Amira Khan: On billing — for reseller setups, does Redwood invoice Celestia or the end customer?
[04:37] Maya Thompson: For reseller flows, Redwood can invoice the partner (Celestia) and you invoice the end customer. For marketplace listings we often do referral/lead share models.
[04:48] Diego Alvarez: We need some details on deployment artifacts — images, helm charts, or operator? We prefer infra-as-code so our automation can provision stacks.
[04:58] Leon Park: We provide Helm charts and Terraform modules for private deployments. For on-prem there's an operator-based install and reference architectures. We'll share links.
[05:10] Amira Khan: Great. A little bit about go-to-market: we can do co-sell for enterprise deals, and Celestia can introduce Redwood to existing EMEA telco customers. We'd want co-branded collateral and joint case studies.
[05:24] Maya Thompson: Sounds aligned. We'll propose a co-sell motion and an MDR (minimum deal registration) process.
[05:30] Priya Nair: Performance benchmarking — we usually ask partners to run a 2-week pilot and provide a baseline report (latency percentile, cost/token, failure modes). Can Redwood support that?
[05:42] Leon Park: Yes, we can run benchmarks. For a partner pilot we typically do an initial run on a small dedicated pool, collect p95/p99 latencies, token costs, and KV cache hit rates. We also provide a template report.
[05:56] Diego Alvarez: Any gotchas with licensing for models? Some customers ask for models with restricted commercial use.
[06:04] Maya Thompson: We'll need to confirm model licensing per case. We maintain a model catalog and note licensing constraints. For partners we can control which model variants are allowed on partner-managed pools.
[06:18] Amira Khan: Ok. A couple of practical asks from our side: 1) Security pack, 2) Partner pricing, 3) Benchmark template, and 4) Example reseller contract.
[06:29] Maya Thompson: Noted. We'll send those items after the call.
[06:33] Priya Nair: Timeline wise — we're targeting a pilot with one anchor customer in Q1 2027. We'd like to have legal and security pre-reads before December.
[06:44] Maya Thompson: That timeline works. We'll aim to get docs over this week and schedule the tech deep dive for Nov 24 — does that work for your infra folks?
[06:52] Diego Alvarez: Nov 24 looks good, please send invites.
[06:56] Leon Park: For the tech deep dive, we'll plan to bring a runtime engineer to discuss kernel choices, quantization profiles, and KV caching strategies. Also, we'll prepare a rough cost model for 8k contexts.
[07:10] Amira Khan: Perfect. Quick question: are there references of other partners running reseller models we can speak to?
[07:16] Maya Thompson: Yes, we have a couple of channel partners in EMEA — I'll include references in the pack.
[07:22] Priya Nair: On data residency — can Redwood attest that customer data never leaves the partner's selected region for private deployments?
[07:31] Leon Park: For private and dedicated pools hosted in your region, we can configure storage and KV caches to remain in-region. We'll need to validate any third-party telemetry egress points.
[07:46] Diego Alvarez: Good to hear. One more technical clarification: can we bring our own AMIs/images to run Redwood software on our fleet?
[07:54] Maya Thompson: In some cases yes, with partner images we provide a validated image spec. For strict air-gapped installs we provide an image bundle you can import.
[08:07] Amira Khan: Great. Anything else from Redwood?
[08:10] Maya Thompson: No, that's it from us. We'll follow up with the doc pack. Thanks for the time.
[08:16] Priya Nair: Thanks, everyone.
[08:18] (meeting ends)
